name: What happens to plumbing and electrical lines during pool removal?

mainEntity.name: What happens to old pool plumbing, gas lines, and electrical wiring when an in-ground pool is removed?
mainEntity.text: What happens to old pool plumbing, gas lines, and electrical wiring when an in-ground pool is removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool removal is not just demolition of the shell. It also requires addressing pumps, filters, underground plumbing, electrical wiring, bonding, lighting circuits, and sometimes gas lines for heaters or fire features. Some components can be removed entirely, while others may be safely abandoned in place if they are no longer active and are properly capped. The key is to identify every line before excavation so the crew does not hit a live utility or leave a hazard behind. In older Los Angeles-area homes, undocumented pool systems are common, which makes pre-demolition review especially important. Homeowners should ask for a clear scope showing what gets removed, what gets capped, and what gets left buried. If the pool area is being repurposed for construction or major landscaping, utility cleanup should be planned carefully so future work is not blocked by hidden lines.
acceptedAnswer.description: Old pool plumbing, electrical, lighting, and gas lines should be safely disconnected, abandoned, or removed as part of the project scope. Some lines can stay buried if they are properly capped and documented, but damaged or active utilities must be handled carefully. The contractor should identify all lines before excavation begins.
